name: The Denver Post editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides Media Bias Rating: Center (news). The board itself describes its members as Post employees separate from the newsroom. In 2026 it opposed both the conservative Amendment 81 and the progressive Amendment 87.

name: The Gazette editorial board (Colorado Springs Gazette and Denver Gazette)
lean_basis: AllSides rates the Colorado Springs Gazette's news coverage Center, but the editorial board is reliably conservative: in 2026 it backed all eleven conservative-sponsored measures and opposed all three progressive ones. The Colorado Springs Gazette and Denver Gazette share one editorial board and publish identical picks, so they are one endorser here.

name: The Colorado Sun
lean_basis: Nonprofit newsroom. Its ethics policy says journalists must not 'create the impression that The Colorado Sun, as an institution, endorses' candidates, parties or initiatives; it publishes explainers, not endorsements.

name: League of Women Voters of Colorado
lean_basis: Nonpartisan civic organization that does not endorse candidates. It does take Support, Oppose or No Stance positions on ballot measures based on its long-standing published policy positions (which include supporting a graduated income tax and opposing TABOR), so its measure stances tend to align with the progressive side on fiscal questions.

name: Colorado Democratic Party
lean_basis: Official state party organization. Positions set by its State Central Committee in May and September 2026.

name: Colorado Republican Party (state party)
lean_basis: Official state party organization. As of October 16, 2026 we could not find any published state-party positions on the 2026 measures; see the Weld County GOP entry for a county-party proxy.

name: Weld County Republican Party
lean_basis: Official county Republican Party. Adopted positions on all 14 statewide measures by resolution on September 15, 2026. Used here because the state party has published no positions.

name: Bell Policy Center
lean_basis: Self-described progressive policy organization; co-leads the Protect Colorado's Future coalition behind Amendment 87.

name: Colorado Fiscal Institute
lean_basis: Progressive fiscal policy group; a lead backer of Amendment 87 and a member of the Protect Colorado's Future coalition.

name: Independence Institute
lean_basis: Self-described free-market think tank. Its 2026 voter guide is paid for by Affordable Colorado, an issue committee registered against Amendment 87 and Proposition NN.

name: Common Sense Institute Colorado
lean_basis: Self-described 'non-partisan research organization dedicated to the protection and promotion of Colorado's economy'; its research is routinely cited by the conservative side (the Gazette calls it nonpartisan; Chalkbeat and the Sun describe it as conservative-leaning). Its 2026 ballot guide publishes analysis and 'bottom line' summaries, not vote recommendations.

name: Colorado Chamber of Commerce
lean_basis: Statewide business association. Its board took positions only on the three tax measures (Amendment 87, Propositions NN and 136), all on the business/anti-tax side.

name: Colorado AFL-CIO
lean_basis: State labor federation. Its 2026 guide endorses only Democratic candidates and supports the two progressive fiscal measures.

name: Conservation Colorado
lean_basis: Self-described 'largest environmental advocacy organization' in the state; endorses candidates (almost all Democrats) and describes the conservative-sponsored measures as coming from 'a network of far-right interests.'

name: ACLU of Colorado
lean_basis: Civil liberties organization; states it is nonpartisan and does not endorse candidates. Its measure positions are limited to civil-rights questions and all five are 'No' on conservative-sponsored measures.

name: Advance Colorado
lean_basis: Self-described 'leading conservative policy and advocacy organization in Colorado.' Its executive director Michael Fields and attorney Suzanne Taheri are the designated representatives of Amendments 81, 82, 85 and 86 and Propositions 132 and 136, and its allied committees Brighter Colorado and 'No on 87, Yes on 136' are registered against Amendment 87 and Proposition NN.

name: Colorado Concern
lean_basis: Alliance of Colorado CEOs that lobbies on business-climate issues. We could not find a published 2026 measure position list as of October 16, 2026.

name: Registered issue committees (official campaign committees for and against each measure)
lean_basis: Not an endorser with a lean. This is the Colorado Secretary of State's official list of the campaign committees registered to support or oppose each measure. Each committee's own lean follows the side it is on.
